brief.summary: Equity futures were slightly higher, with S&P and Nasdaq up as markets tried to rebound from two weeks of losses. Long-end yields were up on the margin, with 10-year near 5% and 30-year around 5.31%; front-end was anchored by expectations the Fed holds Wednesday, though 80% odds of a December hike are priced. Credit spreads are widening, especially for AI/hyperscaler and weaker cloud names, while oil slipped but stayed above $100. The dominant narrative was AI capex versus free cash flow and capital access, compounded by heavy equity issuance and geopolitical risk around Iran and the midterms. Tone was cautious and skeptical despite positive futures.
notable_quotes: Debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money, and companies that don't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers.
It's a great time to prune risk. Bonds are working again.
